_comment: Human-edited narrative. Safe to edit by hand. src/export_portfolio.py merges this with live Alpaca data to produce portfolio.json — never edit portfolio.json directly, CI overwrites it every weekday evening.
disclaimer: Alpaca paper account. Realized figures cover closed trades only and are engineering proof-of-process, not a track record or investment advice.

strategies.name: Clenow Trend Following
strategies.plain: buys shares that have been climbing steadily, and steps aside when the whole market turns
strategies.thesis: Some shares climb steadily for months at a time. This sleeve ranks the market by how smooth a climb has been, not just how big, and buys the steadiest risers while the market overall is still healthy.
rules: A share only qualifies while it is above its long-run average price and close to its highest point of the past year
Calmer shares get more money, jumpier ones get less, so no single holding dominates the risk
If the market as a whole turns down, the sleeve stops buying and sits in cash

evidence.label: Based on Clenow's Stocks on the Move

strategies.name: Ranked Asset Allocation
strategies.plain: moves money between industries once a month, toward whichever ones are leading
strategies.thesis: Once a month it ranks broad industry funds — energy, banks, healthcare and the rest — and shifts money toward the leaders. When conditions look poor it holds defensive assets instead of forcing a bet.

evidence.label: Background: Faber on tactical asset allocation

strategies.name: High Pullback Mean Reversion
strategies.plain: buys solid companies that have fallen unusually far, once falling stops
strategies.thesis: Sometimes a good company is sold off far harder than its situation warrants. This sleeve looks for shares deep below their high point of the past year, checks the business still passes quality tests, and waits for the fall to stop before buying.

evidence.label: Background: De Bondt & Thaler on overreaction

strategies.name: Deep Momentum
strategies.plain: learns which past patterns tend to precede gains, instead of being told a fixed rule
strategies.thesis: Learns its ranking from many measurements at once rather than following one fixed formula. Staying in research until it holds up on data it has never seen.

evidence.label: Based on Lim, Zohren & Roberts, Deep Momentum Networks

strategies.name: Time-Series Momentum
strategies.plain: asks whether each fund itself is trending up, rather than comparing it to others
strategies.thesis: Judges each fund against its own recent history rather than against other funds. Long studied, and simple enough to be a useful yardstick for the more elaborate sleeves.

evidence.label: Based on Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen, Time Series Momentum

strategies.name: Betting Against Beta
strategies.plain: leans toward steadier shares, which historically paid more per unit of risk taken
strategies.thesis: Leans toward shares that move less violently than the market. The published version needs borrowing to work properly, which is why it stays in research here.

evidence.label: Based on Frazzini & Pedersen, Betting Against Beta
